import java.util.*;

public class Main {
    static int MOD;

    static class Mint {
        int value;

        Mint() { value = 0; }
        Mint(long x) { value = normalize(x); }

        static int normalize(long x) {
            int v = (int)(x % MOD);
            if (v < 0) v += MOD;
            return v;
        }

        Mint add(Mint other) {
            int res = value + other.value;
            if (res >= MOD) res -= MOD;
            return new Mint(res);
        }

        Mint subtract(Mint other) {
            int res = value - other.value;
            if (res < 0) res += MOD;
            return new Mint(res);
        }

        Mint multiply(Mint other) {
            long res = (long)value * other.value;
            return new Mint(res);
        }

        Mint divide(Mint other) {
            return multiply(other.inverse());
        }

        Mint inverse() {
            int a = value, m = MOD;
            int u = 0, v = 1;
            while (a != 0) {
                int t = m / a;
                m -= t * a;
                int temp = a; a = m; m = temp;
                u -= t * v;
                temp = u; u = v; v = temp;
            }
            // m should be 1
            return new Mint(u);
        }

        Mint negate() {
            return new Mint(-value);
        }

        @Override
        public String toString() {
            return Integer.toString(value);
        }
    }

    static Mint power(Mint a, long b) {
        Mint res = new Mint(1);
        Mint x = a;
        while (b > 0) {
            if ((b & 1) == 1) res = res.multiply(x);
            x = x.multiply(x);
            b >>= 1;
        }
        return res;
    }

    public static void main(String[] args) {
        Scanner sc = new Scanner(System.in);
        int n = sc.nextInt();
        int m = sc.nextInt();
        MOD = sc.nextInt();

        // Precompute factorials and inverse factorials up to needed size
        int maxSize = Math.max(n, m) + 5; // enough for combinations
        Mint[] fact = new Mint[maxSize];
        Mint[] invFact = new Mint[maxSize];
        fact[0] = new Mint(1);
        invFact[0] = new Mint(1);
        for (int i = 1; i < maxSize; i++) {
            fact[i] = fact[i-1].multiply(new Mint(i));
            invFact[i] = fact[i].inverse();
        }

        // Combination function using precomputed factorials
        // We'll define a function that returns Mint
        // But we need to handle dynamic resizing? Actually we precomputed up to maxSize, which is enough.
        // The original code resized on demand, but we can just use the precomputed arrays.
        // However, the original code used a lambda that resized if needed. Since we precomputed up to max(n,m)+something, it's fine.
        // But note: the original code used C(l+r, l) where l+r can be up to 2*m? Actually in the loops, l+r = i-1, and i goes up to m, so max is m-1. So maxSize = m+5 is enough.
        // For the second part, C(s, add) where s <= m, add <= s, so fine.
        // So we can use the precomputed arrays.

        // Helper function to compute C(x, y)
        // We'll implement as a method that uses fact and invFact.
        // But we need to handle y out of range.
        // We'll create a method inside main.

        // Actually we can define a local class or just inline.
        // Let's define a function using a lambda-like approach? Java 8 has functional interfaces but we can just write a method.

        // We'll compute ptr_ways and ptr_dp arrays of size m+1
        Mint[] ptrWays = new Mint[m+1];
        Mint[] ptrDp = new Mint[m+1];
        ptrWays[0] = new Mint(1);
        for (int i = 1; i <= m; i++) {
            ptrWays[i] = new Mint(0);
            ptrDp[i] = new Mint(0);
            // first loop for ptrWays
            for (int j = 0; j < i; j++) {
                int l = j;
                int r = i - 1 - l;
                Mint comb = C(l + r, l, fact, invFact);
                Mint term = ptrWays[l].multiply(ptrWays[r]).multiply(comb).multiply(new Mint(l + r + 2));
                ptrWays[i] = ptrWays[i].add(term);
            }
            // second loop for ptrDp
            for (int j = 0; j < i; j++) {
                int l = j;
                int r = i - 1 - l;
                Mint comb = C(l + r, l, fact, invFact);
                Mint add = new Mint((long)l * (l + 1) + (long)r * (r + 1)).divide(new Mint(2));
                Mint term1 = ptrWays[l].multiply(ptrWays[r]).multiply(comb).multiply(add);
                ptrDp[i] = ptrDp[i].add(term1);
                Mint term2 = (ptrDp[l].multiply(ptrWays[r]).add(ptrDp[r].multiply(ptrWays[l]))).multiply(comb).multiply(new Mint(l + r + 2));
                ptrDp[i] = ptrDp[i].add(term2);
            }
        }

        // dp and ways tables
        Mint[][] dp = new Mint[n+1][m+1];
        Mint[][] ways = new Mint[n+1][m+1];
        for (int i = 0; i <= n; i++) {
            for (int s = 0; s <= m; s++) {
                dp[i][s] = new Mint(0);
                ways[i][s] = new Mint(0);
            }
        }
        ways[0][0] = new Mint(1);
        for (int i = 1; i <= n; i++) {
            for (int s = 0; s <= Math.min(m, i); s++) {
                if (s == i) {
                    dp[i][s] = ptrDp[s];
                    ways[i][s] = ptrWays[s];
                    continue;
                }
                for (int d = 1; d <= s + 1; d++) {
                    Mint ft = dp[i - d][s + 1 - d];
                    Mint way = ways[i - d][s + 1 - d];
                    int add = d - 1;
                    Mint comb = C(s, add, fact, invFact);
                    ways[i][s] = ways[i][s].add(way.multiply(ptrWays[add]).multiply(comb));
                    Mint term = (way.multiply(ptrDp[add]).add(ptrWays[add].multiply(ft))).multiply(comb);
                    dp[i][s] = dp[i][s].add(term);
                }
            }
        }

        System.out.println(dp[n][m]);
    }

    // Helper method for combination
    static Mint C(int x, int y, Mint[] fact, Mint[] invFact) {
        if (y < 0 || y > x) return new Mint(0);
        return fact[x].multiply(invFact[y]).multiply(invFact[x - y]);
    }
}
